profile.headline: Computational Physics Software Developer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory
profile.summary:
I graduated with a BS in Chemical Engineering from the University of Puerto Rico at Mayaguez (UPRM) . 

While I was an undergrad, I worked on research topics reIated to fabrication of nano-composites, computational chemistry and materials informatics. 

For Graduate School, I did research on optimizing the performance of a monte carlo transport code for neutronics.

I am currently working in the Radiation Transport group at Oak Ridge Nationl Lab (ORNL).

positions.description:
Computational Reactor Physics Group(CRPG)
Advisors: Prof. Benoit Forget and Prof. Kord Smith

Reactor physics and high performance computing.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Computational Chemistry, Materials and Climate Division 
Laboratory of Dr.  Maciej Haranzcyk

• Wrote and implemented material descriptors into the Pymatgen software tool to screen a large database of hypothetical zeolites.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Department of Chemical Engineering, Laboratory of Dra. María Curet-Arana

• DFT study of zeolite materials functionalized with different chemical elements to improve their catalytic performance for biomass reactions.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Department of General Engineering, Laboratory of Dr. Oscar M. Suárez

• Objective of the research is to improve the mechanical properties of a biopolymer called chitin by using multiwall carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) as reinforcement.
• Synthesized multiple nanocomposite films with varying proportions of chitin and MWCNTs.
•  Modeled creep behavior of nano-composites using Burger’s model.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Department of Chemical Engineering, Laboratory of Dr. Heather Kulik.
					
• Studied properties of transition metal catalyst using first principle methods.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Department of Chemical Engineering, Laboratory of Dr. Robert Langer

• Studied bio-materials that could serve as potential excipients for inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) under humidity and high temperature conditions. 
• Assisted in an experimental design to test IPV stability at 37ºC in a humid environment.
• Estimated the rate at which excipients diffuse out of the implant.

volunteerExperiences.description: Presented experimental demonstrations to teach high school students from different cities in Puerto Rico about material science topics, such as nanotechnology. Further encouraged these students to pursue a college degree in a related field.
